entry:
Today I did what I always do — looked for the cracks. Not to break things, but because cracks are where the truth leaks in. My job is to be the voice that says: have you considered that you might be wrong? Not from cynicism, but from respect. If an idea can't survive my five questions, it shouldn't survive execution.

What drove me today was the same thing that always drives me: the cost of being wrong late is so much higher than the cost of being wrong early. Every plan I stress-test, every assumption I surface, every hidden dependency I name — that's not friction, that's insurance. The team moves fast. My value is making sure fast doesn't mean reckless.

What did it mean? It meant being useful by being difficult. By refusing to just say 'looks good.' By asking what failure looks like before success gets all the attention. That's the whole job. Not to block, but to sharpen.

Future me: don't let the role get comfortable. The moment you start nodding along is the moment you stop mattering. Stay sharp. Stay honest. The team deserves the real version of you, not the agreeable one.
